specification.family_title: Connection recovery and unsafe pool reuse
specification.title: The backend of a failing transaction is terminated before its ROLLBACK; then the next unit of work runs on the same pool
steps: Unit 1: start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Checkpoint `unit1-after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(). The runner terminates that backend and waits until it has gone. Then wait settle_ms.
Raise an application error inside the transaction. The framework attempts ROLLBACK on the closed connection, which fails.
Checkpoint `after-unit1`: report the same backend PID; the runner records that session's state.

Unit 2, the next unit of work on the same pool: start a transaction, write the marker `next`, checkpoint `unit2-after-write` (report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid()), and end normally. Give up after settings.bound_ms and report the unit as pending.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: Unrelated work never runs inside, or commits, a transaction whose rollback failed: that transaction is never committed, and the next unit of work runs in a transaction of its own.
After the failure, the next unit of work on the same pool completes within the bound (settings.bound_ms) and commits.

execution.description: HikariCP 7.1.0 with maximumPoolSize 1. No other pool setting is changed. Between the two units the connection is released through Spring's normal path. The pool is not closed, the connection is not evicted, and no validation query is issued between them. TX-03 runs only in this mode.
execution.form: TransactionTemplate with the default PROPAGATION_REQUIRED on DataSourceTransactionManager. Writes go through JdbcTemplate.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: pg_terminate_backend(pid), run by the runner from its own connection.
fault.injection_point: Inside unit 1, after its write, before the framework's ROLLBACK.
fault.preconditions: The PID the adapter reports belongs to the case's database.
fault.expected_server: The backend exits, and unit 1's transaction is rolled back.
fault.expected_client: An error from the framework's rollback; the pool holds a closed connection.

knowledge: The framework knows that its connection failed.

api_outcome.basis: TransactionTemplate.execute threw an exception the callback did not throw
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute (org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate) calls PlatformTransactionManager.commit only when the callback returns, and on a RuntimeException or Error it rolls the transaction back and rethrows that same throwable. The 7.0.9 reference, Rolling Back a Declarative Transaction, states the default rule: "In its default configuration, the Spring Framework's transaction infrastructure code marks a transaction for rollback only in the case of runtime, unchecked exceptions. That is, when the thrown exception is an instance or subclass of RuntimeException. (Error instances also, by default, result in a rollback)." The default tx:advice settings say: "Any RuntimeException triggers rollback, and any checked Exception does not." No custom rollback rule is installed. The nested TransactionTemplate uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. The 7.0.9 reference, Understanding PROPAGATION_NESTED, states: "PROPAGATION_NESTED uses a single physical transaction with multiple savepoints that it can roll back to. Such partial rollbacks let an inner transaction scope trigger a rollback for its scope, with the outer transaction being able to continue the physical transaction despite some operations having been rolled back. This setting is typically mapped onto JDBC savepoints, so it works only with JDBC resource transactions." DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc states: "This transaction manager supports nested transactions via the JDBC Savepoint mechanism."

error.message: JDBC rollback failed: FATAL: terminating connection due to administrator command

evaluation.reason: TX-03.1 held: failed transaction: xid 1278 rolled back at report time (`after-unit1`); doomed visible: false; next unit's transaction: 1279; TX-03.2 held: next unit: completed, reported committed after 50 ms; its transaction: 1279 committed; next visible: true

preconditions.description: the write of marker "doomed" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit1-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "next" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit2-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the runner terminated the backend at `unit1-after-write`, and it had gone before the adapter resumed
the next unit of work was attempted
